newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Tupras says first tanker to load Iraq oil.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Tupras says first tanker to load Iraq oil.

text.p: An official from Turkey's state oil refiner Tupras said the first tanker to load Iraqi crude under the U.N. oil-for-food deal arrived offshore near the Turkish port of Ceyhan on Friday morning.
"The Gole tanker has arrived at Ceyhan and is waiting off shore about one and a half hours from the terminal," the official told Reuters.
He said the vessel would now await instructions for loading but added that the timing of this was not yet clear.

Turkey is planning to hold a ceremony at Ceyhan on Monday to celebrate the resumption of oil flows from the Mediterranean terminal. Turkish oil officials have said the loading could begin before then.

A Tupras spokeswoman said the 150,000-tonne tanker Gole would transport the crude to the Aliaga refinery in the western city of Izmir. Aliaga is owned by Tupras which has U.N. approval of a contract to buy 75,000 barrels per day of Iraqi oil.

She said some of the oil which Tupras was taking under the contract may also be transported to the company's Kirikkale refinery, connected by a 447-km (280-mile) pipeline to Ceyhan. She did not say how much or when crude might be sent this way.
